---
title: The commands
description: Every command of smalldocs and its options.
order: 9
---

Each command takes the project's folder, the one with `_quarto.yml`. It is the folder you are in
when you give none.

## render

```bash
smalldocs render [DIR] [--quiet] [--strict]
```

Build the site. `--quiet` prints only warnings and errors. `--strict` exits with 1 when there is a
warning, such as a broken link or a key that smalldocs ignores.

## preview

```bash
smalldocs preview [DIR] [--port 4200] [--host 127.0.0.1] [--no-browser]
```

Build the site, serve it, and open a browser. On each change to a file of the project, build it
again; the browser reloads. A failed build prints its error and keeps the last good site. It
listens on this machine only, unless you give `--host`.

## check

```bash
smalldocs check [DIR]
```

Build the site into a scratch folder, and list what to look at before you move from Quarto: keys
that smalldocs ignores, broken links, and Markdown that only Pandoc reads. Exit with 1 if there is
anything.

## api

```bash
smalldocs api build|check|list [--dir DIR]
smalldocs api module NAME [--dir DIR]
```

Make the reference pages, check the docments, list the symbols, or print one module as Markdown. See
[The API reference](api.qmd).

## publish

```bash
smalldocs publish gh-pages [DIR] [--branch gh-pages] [--remote origin] [--no-render] [-m MESSAGE]
```

Build the site and push it to the branch, through a temporary worktree. Your working tree and your
branch do not change, and your git hooks do not run on the site's commit. It refuses to publish onto
your current branch, the remote's default branch, `main` or `master`, which hold your sources.
`--no-render` publishes the output folder as it is.

## Exit codes

| Code | Means |
|---|---|
| 0 | Done |
| 1 | Done, with something to fix: `--strict` with warnings, or `check` and `api check` with findings |
| 2 | Stopped: no `_quarto.yml`, a bad option, a failed script, or a port in use |
